\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{میعاد} (mīād)}{میعاد (mīād)}]{\ur{میعاد} (mīād) — a time limit; a term}

\label{lesson:UR-C526-miad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for still standing, then the Urdu for to keep (something) pending.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{میعاد}}
\textbf{\ur{میعاد}} — \emph{mīād} — \textquotedblleft{}a time limit; a term\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{میعاد} \ur{ختم} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{ٹکٹ} \ur{بیکار} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar mīād khatm huī to ṭikaṭ bekār ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the time limit runs out, the ticket will be useless.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{میعاد}} (\emph{mīād}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{mīʿād}, \textquotedblleft{}an appointed time\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mīād}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mīād}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar mīād khatm huī to ṭikaṭ bekār ho gā.} — If the time limit runs out, the ticket will be useless.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for still standing, then the Urdu for to keep (something) pending, then say \emph{mīād} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{میعاد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A time limit; a term\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مقررہ} (muqarrarā)}{مقررہ (muqarrarā)}]{\ur{مقررہ} (muqarrarā) — fixed in advance; set (of a time)}

\label{lesson:UR-C526-muqarrara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to keep (something) pending, then the Urdu for a time limit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مقررہ}}
\textbf{\ur{مقررہ}} — \emph{muqarrarā} — \textquotedblleft{}fixed in advance; set (of a time)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{میچ} \ur{مقررہ} \ur{وقت} \ur{پر} \ur{ہوا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{جائیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar maich muqarrarā vaqt par huā to ham jāeṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the match is held at the set time, we will go.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مقررہ}} (\emph{muqarrarā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{muqarrara}, \textquotedblleft{}fixed, settled\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for saying what happens if.

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to keep (something) pending, then the Urdu for a time limit, then say \emph{muqarrarā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{فوری} (faurī)}{فوری (faurī)}]{\ur{فوری} (faurī) — urgent; immediate}

\label{lesson:UR-C526-fauri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a time limit, then the Urdu for fixed in advance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{فوری}}
\textbf{\ur{فوری}} — \emph{faurī} — \textquotedblleft{}urgent; immediate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar kām faurī hai to maiṅ āj hī karūṅ gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{وقفہ} (vaqfā)}{وقفہ (vaqfā)}]{\ur{وقفہ} (vaqfā) — a break; an interval}

\label{lesson:UR-C526-vaqfa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for fixed in advance, then the Urdu for urgent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{وقفہ}}
\textbf{\ur{وقفہ}} — \emph{vaqfā} — \textquotedblleft{}a break; an interval\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{وقفہ} \ur{ہوا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{چائے} \ur{پئیں} \ur{گے۔}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مکمل} (mukammal)}{مکمل (mukammal)}]{\ur{مکمل} (mukammal) — complete; finished}

\label{lesson:UR-C526-mukammal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for urgent, then the Urdu for a break in work.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مکمل}}
\textbf{\ur{مکمل}} — \emph{mukammal} — \textquotedblleft{}complete; finished\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{کام} \ur{مکمل} \ur{ہوا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{کل} \ur{چھٹی} \ur{کریں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar kām mukammal huā to ham kal chhuṭṭī kareṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the work is finished, we will take tomorrow off.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مکمل}} (\emph{mukammal}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{mukammal}, \textquotedblleft{}made complete\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
